public-preprovider-validation@1.name: Public pre-provider validation
public-preprovider-validation@1.rationale: For a public configuration-validation claim whose authored semantics require deterministic failure before provider execution, sufficient assurance must prove both the public-system outcome and the lower-level validation rules without requiring a live provider call that the requirement explicitly says must not happen.

cadence.description: Re-evaluate on the retained required CI verification run.

obligations.label: Component validation path
obligations.rationale: The authored verification intent requires direct validation-rule evidence below the public scenario layer.

obligations.label: Public-system validation path
obligations.rationale: The public error contract must be exercised through the router while remaining pre-provider.

obligations.label: Independent verification methods
obligations.rationale: The verification intent explicitly combines a public behavioral scenario with direct lower-level validation checks.

obligations.label: Component mutation reach
obligations.rationale: Pilot policy floor: most generated faults in the declared validation scope should be exercised by the direct validation suite.

obligations.label: Component mutation sensitivity
obligations.rationale: Pilot policy floor: faults actually reached by the direct validation suite should usually be detected by its assertions.

obligations.label: System mutation reach
obligations.rationale: The public behavioral path should traverse most mutation sites in the declared validation scope.

obligations.label: System mutation sensitivity
obligations.rationale: The public behavioral oracle should detect faults that it reaches in the validation implementation.

obligations.label: Specification/model fault challenge
obligations.rationale: The executable scenario outcome must reject a plausible wrong public error category.

obligations.label: Architecture boundary fault challenge
obligations.rationale: Configuration validation must remain in the lower config layer and must not gain a dependency on provider execution code.

obligations.label: Provider-interface isolation challenge
obligations.rationale: Invalid model configuration must fail before any provider HTTP interaction.

obligations.label: Runtime/dependency isolation challenge
obligations.rationale: Injected provider-network degradation must not affect a pre-provider configuration error.

obligations.label: Implementation fault challenge
obligations.rationale: The declared implementation scope must be mutation-challenged with native operator metadata.

optional_improvements.label: Add another independent lower-level oracle
optional_improvements.rationale: A property-oriented validation method could corroborate the existing unit checks, but it is not required by the current profile because the public BDD path already supplies an independent behavioral oracle.

internal-state@1.name: Internal state invariant
internal-state@1.rationale: For a purely internal state invariant, assurance should stay on the actual implementation and deterministic local behavior. A provider network call does not strengthen proof of per-provider/key state isolation, conservative interval selection, or reset-after-success semantics.

cadence.description: Re-evaluate direct invariant checks on the retained required CI run; mutation strength is refreshed by the mutation campaign cadence.

obligations.label: Direct internal-state path
obligations.rationale: The requirement is an internal LimiterState invariant and is most directly demonstrated on the actual component implementation.

obligations.label: At least one direct verification method
obligations.rationale: A deterministic direct verification method is sufficient for this narrow internal invariant; extra methods remain optional corroboration.

obligations.label: Covered-mutant Test Strength
obligations.rationale: Pilot policy floor for the retained mutmut metric: linked tests should kill at least 80% of covered valid mutants. This is killed/(killed+survived), not full-scope Mutation Reach.

optional_improvements.label: Property-based state-transition checks
optional_improvements.rationale: Could explore more provider/key/update sequences without changing the required external-boundary level.

external-provider-compatibility@1.name: External provider compatibility
external-provider-compatibility@1.rationale: A provider-facing compatibility claim needs both deterministic repeatable coverage and periodic evidence against the mutable real dependency. Replay proves stable known interactions; a release-time Direct-live path detects provider drift that replay cannot observe.

cadence.description: Replay evidence is continuous CI; Direct-live compatibility is a pre-release obligation.

freshness.description: A release candidate must have retained Direct-live evidence from the release verification window; no historical live result may be silently reused.

obligations.label: Deterministic cross-provider replay
obligations.rationale: The public asynchronous workflow must continuously exercise provider-facing request/response semantics across supported provider families using repeatable retained interactions.

obligations.label: Release-time real-provider compatibility
obligations.rationale: Provider APIs are mutable external dependencies; replay alone cannot demonstrate that the current adapters still interoperate with the current real services before release.

obligations.label: Public behavioral verification method
obligations.rationale: Compatibility must be demonstrated through the public asynchronous behavior, not only by source or adapter-local checks.

optional_improvements.label: Raise VCR replay credibility above L0
optional_improvements.rationale: Record intended use, cassette pedigree and calibrated comparison to live behavior so replay fidelity can be trusted more strongly between release-time live checks.

REQ_INVALID_CONFIGURATION_ERRORS.source: policy-derived from authored Statement + Verification intent
REQ_INVALID_CONFIGURATION_ERRORS.rationale: The requirement explicitly says invalid configuration is rejected deterministically before provider execution, and its verification intent explicitly calls for both a public API scenario and direct lower-level validation checks. Direct-live provider evidence is therefore not a required target for this claim.

history.reason: Initial explicit Assurance Target introduced by the P30 pilot after replacing generic inferred gaps with Target minus Actual evaluation.

TREQ_RATE_LIMIT_STATE.source: policy-derived from authored Statement + Verification intent
TREQ_RATE_LIMIT_STATE.rationale: The claim is entirely about LimiterState behavior inside llm-router. Direct-live provider interaction is neither required nor promoted as a gap; the meaningful weakness is the retained covered-mutant Test Strength of the linked internal-state tests.

history.reason: Added as the internal-state counterexample to prove that Direct-live is not a universal assurance target.

REQ_ASYNC_PROVIDER_EXECUTION.source: policy-derived from authored Statement + Verification intent
REQ_ASYNC_PROVIDER_EXECUTION.rationale: The claim explicitly spans supported provider families through the public asynchronous router. Repeatable VCR evidence is required continuously, while a pre-release Direct-live obligation is required to detect drift in mutable external provider APIs.

history.reason: Added as the provider-facing counterexample where a Direct-live assurance obligation is justified rather than inferred globally.
